name: Modal
hint: Open it: the dialog grows out of the button and shrinks back into it.
description: Dialog that grows out of the button that opened it and shrinks back on close, over a dimmed, blurred background. It holds any content: a title, a description, your children as the body and a footer of actions. Focus trap, inert page behind, Escape, press outside, scroll lock, and focus goes back to the trigger (or somewhere sensible if the trigger is gone).
intents: dialog with custom content and actions
usage: Use for short, focused tasks that block the page (invite, confirm, edit one thing). Pass `title`, `description` and the body as `children`; the default footer is Cancel plus one confirm button wired to `onConfirm` (return false to keep it open, or a promise to show loading until it settles). Pass `footer` for your own actions or `footer={null}` for none. It opens from its own trigger button by default; pass `trigger` as your own element or `(props) => <Button {...props} />`, or `trigger={null}` and control it with `open` / `onOpenChange`. Set `busy` while your own save runs: the confirm button shows loading and the dialog cannot be closed until you clear it. If the trigger can disappear (a delete that removes its row), pass `returnFocusTo`. `closeOnEscape` / `closeOnOutside` switch off those exits. Keep one primary action. For long forms or browsing, use a Drawer.

screenReader: A dialog with aria-modal, named by `title` (by `triggerLabel` when there is no title) and described by `description`; the page behind is inert while it is open. The trigger reports aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded; while busy the dialog is aria-busy and the confirm button is announced as working.

dataProps.type: element | ((props: { ref: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>; onClick: () => void; "aria-haspopup": "dialog"; "aria-expanded": boolean; disabled?: boolean }) => node) | null
dataProps.description: Your own trigger: an element (cloned with a ref, onClick and aria attributes), or (props) => node spreading { ref, onClick, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, disabled }. The dialog grows from it. Left out, a built-in button labelled `triggerLabel` is shown, unless you pass `open`: a dialog opened by state has no built-in button. null always renders none.
Label of the built-in trigger button; also the dialog's name when there is no title.
Icon name on the built-in trigger button, or "none".
Disables the trigger so the dialog can't be opened from it.

dataProps.type: RefObject<HTMLElement> | HTMLElement | string | (() => RefObject<HTMLElement> | HTMLElement | string | null) | false
dataProps.description: Where focus goes on close: a ref, an element, a CSS selector or a function returning one. Default: the trigger, else what had focus before opening, else the control nearest to where the trigger was. false leaves focus alone.
The dialog element (null while closed). className, style and other props go to it too.
Any other attribute (id, aria-*, data-*) goes to the dialog panel, a <div>, and so do className and style, merged with the panel's own.
